title: Jensen Huang says he would return as Nvidia CEO if the board asked
dek: Huang, who resigned last week, signals willingness to come back while Nvidia’s board says it does not plan to reinstate him.
body:
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive last week, says he would be willing to return as CEO if the company’s board of directors wanted him to, he said in a statement reported by The Wall Street Journal. Huang added that “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers,” according to The Verge’s reporting of the WSJ coverage.

Nvidia’s board has publicly said it does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO, according to The Verge and TechCrunch. The company is continuing to operate with other executives in place while the situation remains unsettled.

## Why it matters

Nvidia is central to the current AI market, and leadership changes at the company affect investors, customers, and partners. BBC coverage underscores Nvidia’s importance to the U.S. economy. CNBC has highlighted how Nvidia’s management team, including CFO Colette Kress, shows the company remains at the center of AI despite Huang’s departure.

A reappointment or prolonged leadership dispute would matter for capital markets, customer confidence, and ongoing commercial partnerships that depend on Nvidia’s products and road map.

## The details

- Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO last week; he now says he would return if the board wanted him, according to a statement reported by The Wall Street Journal and summarized by The Verge.
- Nvidia’s board has said the company does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO, according to reporting by The Verge and TechCrunch.
- The Verge reported Huang’s remark that he has received an “outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers” since his departure.
- BBC has placed Nvidia and Huang in the context of U.S. economic importance; CNBC has noted Nvidia’s continued centrality to AI under other executives including Colette Kress.
- The Wall Street Journal, TechCrunch, BBC, and CNBC are among outlets covering the developments; details about the board’s internal deliberations, the reasons for Huang’s resignation, and any timeline for a formal vote or decision have not been disclosed in the cited reporting.

## What to watch

Watch for an official statement from Nvidia’s board about succession plans or a formal decision on Huang’s status; the company’s public comments so far say it does not plan to reinstate him. Monitor filings or investor communications for any changes that would affect market expectations and customer contracts.

Also follow reporting from the Wall Street Journal, The Verge, TechCrunch, BBC, and CNBC for updates on board deliberations, executive actions by Nvidia’s leadership team, and any reactions from major customers or investors.

Source: reporting by The Verge.
author: Kelvane Club Desk
